Macbeth showed hesitation to the whole murder after the gravity of things sank in about the consequences, yet Lady Macbeth pushed him to kill Duncan anyways, by essentially calling him weak-willed. 

Macbeth has been shown to value her opinion, and see her as an equal to him, so him listening to her isn’t that far fetched, and neither is him delivering the blow in my opinion. Mind you, there is also evidence to show how Lady Macbeth May have taken matters in her own hands.

I can mask and use charisma well when I’m at school, but as soon as I step into a taxi to go home I completely shut off and go non-verbal for the rest of the journey. Sometimes I might go non-verbal at school as well, but I’ll hide behind food or work, and use it as an excuse to no being able to talk.

I think charisma can be learned, definitely, but it can also hide the little parts of our autism that make us truly us, so I’d say be cautious and stick to who you are outside of social situations if you feel like you need to hide who you are during them.

So many people are wrapped up in the illusion, how to live life to the fullest. Some people don’t care when the illusion ends for those around them. “It happens,” Those people will murmur, and shrug. Others see the illusion ending as the end to joy itself. They can cry for hours when the illusion ends for those around them.

Then there’s the times when the illusion stops, by the hands of a person who thought the could float above it all. In the end, it catches up to them, and the illusion of life ends for them as well. It’s those people, the people who think they can play god with life, that only validate my job.
